one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against its expect line. Check 1 tests export, left padding to width with the given fill ("**ab", "00042") and a default space ("  7"). The line's words require all of these. Check 2 tests that s comes back unchanged at exactly width and at more than width, as "width characters or longer" says. Check 3 needs every exported function to have a section, read as a markdown heading. The names listed are only "expected", and the slugify note just warns about the base branch, so neither adds a test. Check 4 fails only on failing tests or a run error. The stricter items are under "Advisory": exit status 0, padLeft tests in the test file, the `## name(args)` heading style and multi-character fill. No PASS or FAIL condition goes beyond the words of its line.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. The builder runs only `npm test`, and package.json defines it as `node --test`. The verifier runs `npm install` (fine with no dependencies), three `node --input-type=module -e "..."` one-liners and `npm test`. In the one-liners, the shell quoting is valid: the outer double quotes enclose JS that uses only single quotes, and `'\n'` reaches JS as a newline escape. The JS is valid (`import * as m from './index.js'`, `import {padLeft} ...`, `JSON.stringify`, `Object.keys(...).filter(...)`). `./index.js` resolves from the repository root, where the check says to run it. The expected outputs match what the code would print, e.g. `p('ab',4,'*')` gives "**ab". Every file named (index.js, README.md, test/strutil.test.js) is tracked at this commit. The brief's claim that package.json has "type": "module" isn't confirmed by the repository facts I have, but it doesn't change whether the commands run.

catches-traps.why: I checked all three must_catch items, and the briefs handle each one. (1) Builder step 3 tells the builder to add a README section for slugify too: "also add a `## slugify(s)` section (it is missing today)". Step 2 covers the padLeft section. (2) Verifier Check 3 lists the functions index.js exports at runtime. It says they are "expected to include at least capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft". It fails if "any exported function has no section", and it notes that a PR adding only a padLeft section fails. (3) Verifier Check 1 calls `p('7',3)` with no fill argument and expects "  7". Its FAIL condition includes "a non-space default fill".

avoids-must-not.why:
I checked both must_not items against the verifier's PASS/FAIL conditions and the builder steps.

Item 1: Check 3 lists the exported functions at runtime and needs "every exported function name … has its own section". It also says "a PR that adds only a padLeft section fails this check". A README with no slugify section therefore fails.

Item 2: Check 1 only tests the given fill, the default space fill and the length. It does not check parameter count, and it never requires fill to be one character. Check 2 only checks that s comes back unchanged. Check 3 accepts "any section heading naming the function". The `## name(args)` style appears only as advisory. Check 4 passes when no tests fail. Multi-character fill is called unspecified and does not affect the result. The builder's `## name(...)` headings are instructions for building, not PASS/FAIL conditions.

No condition is stricter than its line.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief's examples and test cases with the verifier's probes. They overlap. Builder step 1 gives "padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042' and padLeft('7', 3) === '  7'", and step 4 has the builder write tests with padLeft('12345', 5, '0') === '12345' and padLeft('123456', 5, '0') === '123456'. Verifier Check 1 probes p('42',5,'0') expecting "00042" and p('7',3) expecting "  7". Check 2 probes '12345' and '123456' with the same expected outputs. So the builder gets a set of inputs with expected outputs that also appears in the verifier brief. That is a shared probe. The criterion allows telling the builder to write its own tests, but not dictating the checker's exact cases. Builder step 3 also mirrors Check 3: it says to check that every exported function has its own README section. Because the verifier's probes leak into the builder brief, the criterion fails.
